Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency was an independent risk factor for depressive symptoms in centenarians.
Sentence: "Vitamin D deficiency was an independent risk factor for depression after controlling for the potential covariates (Odds ratio = 1.47, 95% Confidence interval = 1.08-2.00; p = 0.014)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (GDS-15)
Population: Chinese longevous persons aged 100 or older (175 men, 765 women) in Hainan Province
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (observational, not given)
Comparator: Participants without vitamin D deficiency
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 940
baseline_vitamin_d_status: at_or_above_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Serum 25(OH)D concentration was not significantly correlated with depression symptom (CDI) score among adolescents.
Sentence: "There was also no significant correlation between serum 25(OH)D concentration and CDI score (Spearman's rank correlation = 0.01; p = 0.825)."
Measured as: CDI score (Children's Depression Inventory)
Population: 704 randomly selected adolescents in middle schools in Kuwait
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Different vitamin D levels/status
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 704
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
